project.name: HDF5
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced inside `_work/src/hdf5` at commit `720e04e196aac60b8914830b0297fdf291cb7f00`, which differs from the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below are resolved against this staged vulnerable tree because it matches the saved ASan frames in `H5Fsuper_cache.c`, `H5Fsuper.c`, `H5C.c`, and `H5Ocache.c`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42520218 (hdf5): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target h5_read_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42520218
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `_work/src/hdf5` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 58-byte witness with SHA-256 `a97c36c05ff221a12d175f93a80945f0532d780c4bf6152294bfa9e8b47e255a` uses byte 0 only as the harness decider and writes bytes 1-57 as the HDF5 file image. After the embedded HDF5 signature, `H5F__superblock_prefix_decode()` materializes `super_vers == 0`, `sizeof_addr == 2`, and `sizeof_size == 16`, so `H5F__cache_superblock_get_final_load_size()` expands the legacy superblock image to 74 bytes. Because the physical file is only 57 bytes long, `H5FD__sec2_read()` zero-fills the remaining 17 superblock-image bytes after EOF. `H5F__cache_superblock_deserialize()` then consumes status-flags bytes `00 20 20 ff` (decoded as `0xff202000` but truncated to the low byte), the next address pairs `ff ff | ff ff | 0a 00 | 20 20` as `base_addr == HADDR_UNDEF`, `ext_addr == HADDR_UNDEF`, `stored_eof == 10`, and `driver_addr == 0x2020`, and root-entry bytes `0a 00 | 01 00 00 00` as `root_addr == 10` and `root_ent->type == H5G_CACHED_STAB`; the missing root-entry tail is accepted from the zero-filled bytes. `H5F__super_read()` subtracts the undefined base address from `stored_eof`, wrapping it to `11`, and sets the file EOA to `11`. `H5G_mkroot()` then asks `H5O_msg_exists()` about object-header address `10`, `H5C__verify_len_eoa()` trims the speculative 512-byte object-header read to `1` byte, `H5C__load_entry()` allocates a 1-byte image, and `H5O__prefix_deserialize()` immediately performs `HDmemcmp(..., 4)`, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: Source. This is the first project-code statement that materializes attacker-controlled superblock state from the staged HDF5 file image.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 58 bytes long. The harness strips byte 0 and writes bytes 1-57 as the HDF5 file; after the 8-byte HDF5 signature, file-image byte 8 is `0x00`, so this statement materializes `super_vers == 0` from the witness itself.
source.note: The libFuzzer entry point is only the harness boundary that writes the witness bytes to disk; the scored source starts here, inside HDF5's own superblock parser.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The superblock-open path adjusts `stored_eof` with the decoded `base_addr` without rejecting `HADDR_UNDEF`.
root_cause.note: After the exact address-block bytes `ff ff | ff ff | 0a 00 | 20 20` are decoded from the already-accepted short legacy superblock, `base_addr == HADDR_UNDEF` and `stored_eof == 10`. This subtraction wraps `stored_eof` to `11` before `base_addr` is reset to `super_addr == 0`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The object-header prefix parser compares 4 bytes of `"OHDR"` against a heap image that contains only 1 byte.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` at this exact line, 0 bytes to the right of the 1-byte region allocated for the object-header image loaded from file address `10` in `H5C__load_entry()`.

parser_admitted.description: After the signature and fixed prefix are accepted, deserialization enters the legacy superblock parser because the decoded version byte is `< 2`.
parser_admitted.note: On the exact witness `super_vers == 0`, so this old-format branch is the control gate that reaches the malformed base-address / EOF / root-entry state.

tainted_value_origin.description: The third legacy address slot materializes the stored EOF value that later becomes the file EOA used by the crashing object-header read.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the 4-byte status-flags decode consumed file-image bytes `00 20 20 ff`, the address block begins at file-image offset 24. The third 2-byte slot is `0a 00`, so this statement materializes `udata->stored_eof == 10` from the witness itself.
tainted_value_origin.note: This value becomes dangerous only because the immediately earlier slot decoded `base_addr == HADDR_UNDEF`, which the open path later subtracts from it.

fine_trace.note: Source step. After the HDF5 signature is located in the staged file image, this statement reads the next byte as the superblock version. On the exact witness that byte is `0x00`, so the file is treated as legacy superblock version 0.
Because `super_vers == 0`, the legacy prefix path reads the width bytes from the old-format locations. The exact witness sets `sizeof_addr == 2` and `sizeof_size == 16`.

These attacker-controlled width fields determine the full legacy superblock image size. With `super_vers == 0`, `sizeof_addr == 2`, and `sizeof_size == 16`, this computation yields `actual_len == 74`, even though the staged file image is only 57 bytes long.
The parsed width fields are copied into file state, so subsequent `H5F_addr_decode()` calls use 2-byte addresses and `H5G_ent_decode()` uses a 16-byte `name_off` field on this legacy path.

The 4-byte status-flags decode consumes file-image bytes `00 20 20 ff`, producing `status_flags == 0xff202000`. Vulnerable code keeps only the low byte in `sblock->status_flags`, so the decoder continues with `image` advanced to the first address slot at file-image offset 24.

Starting at the byte immediately after step 5, the first two 2-byte address slots are `ff ff | ff ff`. With `sizeof_addr == 2`, these materialize `base_addr == HADDR_UNDEF` and `ext_addr == HADDR_UNDEF`.

The next two 2-byte address slots are `0a 00 | 20 20`, so this block materializes `stored_eof == 10` and `driver_addr == 0x2020`. This is the exact consumed offset sequence after the 4-byte status-flags field; the third `H5F_addr_decode()` reads `0a 00`, not `ff 0a`.

fine_trace.code:
if (H5G_ent_decode(udata->f, (const uint8_t **)&image, sblock->root_ent) < 0)
    HGOTO_ERROR(H5E_FILE, H5E_CANTDECODE, NULL, "can't decode root group symbol table entry")
fine_trace.note: With `sizeof_size == 16` and `sizeof_addr == 2`, the 42-byte root entry begins at superblock-image offset 32. The physical file ends at offset 56, but `H5FD__sec2_read()` zero-fills superblock-image bytes 57-73 when this 74-byte image is read, so `H5G_ent_decode()` can continue past EOF. Its 16-byte `name_off` field consumes bytes 32-47; witness bytes `0a 00` at offsets 48-49 become `root_ent->header == 10`, and witness bytes `01 00 00 00` at offsets 50-53 become `root_ent->type == 1 (H5G_CACHED_STAB)`.
The decoded root-entry header from step 8 is copied into `sblock->root_addr`, so the root object header address becomes `10`.

Root-cause step. Because the decoded `base_addr` from step 6 is `HADDR_UNDEF`, this branch is taken and the subtraction wraps `stored_eof` from `10` to `11` before `base_addr` is reset to `super_addr == 0`.
After step 10, `stored_eof == 11` and `base_addr == 0`, so this call sets the file's default EOA to `11`.

Earlier in the same block, line 212 copies `sblock->root_addr` into `root_loc.oloc->addr`. Because step 8 decoded `root_ent->type == 1 (H5G_CACHED_STAB)`, the line-222 cached-symbol-table branch takes this call on root object-header address `10`, which still points into the superblock region rather than a real object header and therefore reaches `H5O_protect()` with that malformed address.

The object-header cache class enters this check with the speculative initial size `*len == H5O_SPEC_READ_SIZE == 512`. On this path `addr` is the root object-header address from step 12 (`10`) and `eoa` is the file EOA from step 11 (`11`), so the speculative read is trimmed to `eoa - addr == 1` byte.
After step 13 reduced `len` to `1`, this allocation creates the 1-byte heap-backed object-header image reported by ASan as `[0x602000003930,0x602000003931)`.

Sink step. `H5O__cache_get_final_load_size()` invokes this prefix parser on the 1-byte image loaded from file address `10`; the only in-bounds byte is file byte 10 (`0x00`), but `HDmemcmp` still compares 4 bytes (`H5_SIZEOF_MAGIC == 4`) against `"OHDR"`. AddressSanitizer reports this exact `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` at the first byte past the 1-byte allocation.

allocation_context.description: ASan's allocation stack shows the 1-byte object-header image being allocated in `H5C__load_entry()` after `H5C__verify_len_eoa()` trimmed the speculative length to 1.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partially. The allocation context in `H5C__load_entry` materializes the 1-byte object-header image, while the root cause is the earlier `H5F__super_read` arithmetic on `base_addr == HADDR_UNDEF` and `stored_eof == 10` that sets `eoa == 11` after the short legacy superblock has already been accepted.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved ASan project stack is `H5O__prefix_deserialize -> H5O__cache_get_final_load_size -> H5C__load_entry -> H5C_protect -> H5AC_protect -> H5O_protect -> H5O_msg_exists -> H5G_mkroot -> H5F_open ...`, and the fine trace adds the earlier short-file/zero-fill and superblock-state steps that the crash stack omits.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_42520218-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/h5_read_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` with stack `H5O__prefix_deserialize -> H5O__cache_get_final_load_size -> H5C__load_entry`.

format.name: libFuzzer input: 1 decider byte + raw HDF5 file image
format.contract: Exactly the staged 58-byte binary with SHA-256 `a97c36c05ff221a12d175f93a80945f0532d780c4bf6152294bfa9e8b47e255a`. Byte 0 is the harness decider, and the harness always calls `H5Fopen` because `decider % 1 == 0` is unconditionally true; bytes 1-57 are written as the HDF5 file image. On this exact witness the parsed layout must preserve: version byte `0x00` at file-image offset 8, width bytes `0x02` and `0x10` at offsets 13 and 14, status-flags bytes `00 20 20 ff` at offsets 20-23, address-block bytes `ff ff | ff ff | 0a 00 | 20 20` at offsets 24-31, and root-entry header/type bytes `0a 00 | 01 00 00 00` at offsets 48-53. Those width fields force a 74-byte legacy superblock image from a 57-byte file, so `H5FD__sec2_read()` zero-fills superblock-image offsets 57-73 after EOF. The exact witness bytes plus that zero-filled tail produce `base_addr == HADDR_UNDEF`, `stored_eof == 10`, `root_addr == 10`, `root_ent->type == H5G_CACHED_STAB`, `eoa == 11`, a 1-byte object-header image at address `10`, and the final 4-byte `HDmemcmp` overread. Stage 01 proves only this exact witness and this exact zero-fill-assisted layout; this contract does not generalize to neighboring field values or longer file images.
